title: auth handshake — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: First message of every AFB WebSocket connection, replacing the legacy `{type: "auth"}` / `{type: "auth_ok"}` / `{type: "auth_error"}`. Same convention as the other schema-first afbws channels: routed by `channel` (`auth`) then by a mandatory `schema` id, no `type` field; ONE schema id `afbws.auth.v1` is the request, its response (echoes `request_id`) and the server push (no `request_id`); response-only fields are forbidden in a request. Failure: `afbws.auth.error.v1`. Negotiation caveat: `support` is learned only from the auth response, i.e. AFTER the client has already chosen the form of its first message — so the frontend ALWAYS sends afbws.auth.v1, and the backend accepts BOTH the legacy `type: "auth"` and this schema, answering in the form of the request (legacy request -> legacy auth_ok/auth_error; schema request -> afbws.auth.v1 / afbws.auth.error.v1). The backend still lists `afbws.auth.v1` in `support` so a client can tell that the backend understands the new form. Removal of the legacy form is a separate decision. See AFB/docs/API_REGISTRY.md.

auth.title: afbws.auth.v1 — handshake (request / response / server push).
auth.description: Request (client -> server, first message; no `user_id`): `request_id`, `support`, `version`, optional `session_id`. The session is taken from the `afb_session` cookie, or from `session_id` when the cookie is absent/invalid (iframe). `version` (frontend build) is logged for monitoring only — never parsed, compared or used to gate behaviour; all behaviour is gated on `support` alone. Response (same `request_id`): `user_id`, `timezone`, `brokers`, `support`, `access`; `support` — the backend's own declared afbws capability ids (not the intersection; the client computes it). Push (no `request_id`): the whole response, sent when the effective `access` of the connection changes; the client replaces its auth state.

support.description: afbws capability ids (x-afbws-support-id values): in a request — what the client supports; in a response/push — what the backend supports.

version.description: Request only: frontend build version, logged only.

session_id.description: Request only: HTTP session id, used when the cookie is unavailable.

timezone.description: Response/push only: IANA timezone name of the platform (market time on the frontend, e.g. `Europe/Moscow`).

brokers.description: Response/push only: known broker ids for the link connector-create form, sent unconditionally.

error.title: afbws.auth.error.v1 — failed handshake (server -> client); the server closes the socket right after it.
error.description: `unauthorized` — no valid session (close code 4001); `session_invalid` — the session exists but its access profile could not be resolved (close code 4001); `invalid_request` — the first message is not a valid auth request (close code 4000). `request_id` echoes the request's when it could be read.
